raised_by: PI review of the utilization probe.

THE_OVERCLAIM_BEING_CORRECTED.as_written: the amended record stated that if geometry is barely used at inference, then 'the extra 1,000,000 steps are the remaining explanation' for delta_A, and that the continuation control is therefore 'the decisive experiment'.
THE_OVERCLAIM_BEING_CORRECTED.why_that_is_wrong: it is a FALSE DICHOTOMY. It treats 'entity geometry matters' and 'extra training time matters' as the only two candidates, and implicitly equates 'geometry is unused at inference' with 'geometry did nothing'. Those are not the same claim.
THE_OVERCLAIM_BEING_CORRECTED.the_omitted_third_hypothesis: GEOMETRY AS LEARNING SCAFFOLD. The entity pathway may have mattered DURING OPTIMIZATION -- supplying gradient signal that steered the policy into a different basin / different solution -- and then become largely redundant at inference once the base CNN/vec pathway had reorganized around that solution. A scaffold can be load-bearing while it is being built and near-inert once the structure stands. Under this hypothesis the +1M steps and the entity stream are NOT competing explanations: the entity stream is what made those particular 1M steps productive.
THE_OVERCLAIM_BEING_CORRECTED.what_this_means_for_the_probe_s_status: the utilization probe remains valid and unchanged as a measurement -- the entity pathway IS small at inference, symmetrically across pi_A3 and pi_B3. What is retracted is the causal inference drawn from it.

SECOND_LIMITATION_OF_THE_PROBE_now_recor.issue: the probe measured ONE-STEP behavioural divergence on states generated by the INTACT policy. Both the KL and the greedy-action-agreement statistics are computed on a state distribution that the full policy itself produced.
SECOND_LIMITATION_OF_THE_PROBE_now_recor.why_that_matters: a 3% per-decision difference is not a 3% outcome difference. Under closed-loop control, a small number of changed decisions alters the subsequent trajectory, which changes the states encountered, which can compound. On-policy one-step agreement systematically UNDERSTATES the closed-loop consequence of an intervention.
SECOND_LIMITATION_OF_THE_PROBE_now_recor.consequence: '97% action agreement' must not be read as '3% behavioural effect'. It bounds the per-decision footprint, not the episode-level effect.

CORRECTED_CLAIM_STRUCTURE.established_by_the_probe: the entity pathway has a small per-decision footprint at inference, and that footprint is symmetric between the passing (pi_A3) and failing (pi_B3) regimes -- so the crossover asymmetry is not explained by an entity-utilization asymmetry. The B-only 'didn't use the geometry enough' hypothesis is PARKED.
NOT_established_by_the_probe: that geometry is performance-irrelevant at inference (closed-loop untested)
that geometry did not cause the specialization to emerge during training (scaffold hypothesis untested)
that training duration is the explanation for delta_A
three_live_hypotheses_for_delta_A: H1 geometry load-bearing at inference: the sparse changed decisions are pivotal and carry the Pole-A gap
H2 geometry as scaffold: mattered during learning, largely redundant at inference
H3 training duration: the extra 1,000,000 steps would have produced the gap with or without the entity stream

which_experiment_separates_which.POLE_A_GEOMETRY_ABLATION (next, cheap, n: separates H1 from {H2, H3}. Tests inference-time load-bearing only.
which_experiment_separates_which.no-entity +1M continuation control (expe: separates H2 from H3. Only worth spending AFTER the ablation rules H1 in or out.

STATUS_OF_THE_PARKED_B_ONLY_HYPOTHESIS: PARKED, not refuted-in-general: the probe shows no utilization gap between the regimes, which removes the specific mechanism 'B failed because it underused geometry'. Pole B may still differ from Pole A for other reasons (observation ambiguity under lock_defender/2v1, or pi_A3 generalizing strongly enough to erase the contrast). Those remain open but are no longer the next step.
